O.outcome_detail: apology WDCT performance rated for correct expressions, quality of information, strategy choices, and politeness

cells.quote: Regarding the first scenario, the mean scores in the pre-test and posttest were significantly different in three areas; “correct expressions,” “quality of information,” and “strategy choices” (p value <.05) with no significant difference in “politeness.” Similarly, no significant difference in the same criterion was found when students apologized to their neighbor as well as that of “quality of information” (p value>.05). However, the mean scores were significantly different in “correct expressions” and “strategy choices.”
cells.note: Some apology criteria improved significantly, while others showed no significant difference; the study did not report an equivalence test or adequate power.

O.outcome_detail: stakeholder prioritization of training topics

cells.quote: IWLC prioritized non-pharmacological treatments, noting that many medications addressed only some symptoms and often resulted in polypharmacy, adverse side effects, and high costs. While PCPs and experts agreed that non-pharmacologic treatments should be the initial approach, they felt that education should place greater emphasis on pharmacologic options, as PCPs are less familiar with available medications, their off-label uses, and associated risks and benefits.
cells.note: The study reports stakeholder-group differences in perceived training priorities, not an educational intervention effect.

O.outcome_detail: self-reported availability of PCI emergency bailout equipment

cells.quote: Over 93% of operators had access to covered stents, temporary pacing, pericardiocentesis, echocardiography and vasopressor drugs. However, there was significantly reduced availability of coronary/aortic snares and coronary coils, with availability rates of 65.7%, 59.4%, and 50.9%, respectively.
cells.note: Survey-based comparison of reported equipment availability; no instructional treatment was compared.
